analysis.title: Eversource Energy (ES): First Take: Slight EPS beat versus GSe and consensus; regulatory catalysts in focus
key_insights: ES (Buy) reported 3Q2026 adjusted EPS of $0.92 versus GSe $0.91 and FactSet consensus $0.90. The beat was slight.
2026 EPS guidance moved from $4.57-$4.72 to $4.62-$4.70. The new midpoint of $4.66 is below GSe of $4.68.

Versus GSe, lower gross margin was offset by lower operating expenses (O&M and D&A) and lower income taxes. Exhibit 1 shows revenue of $2,979mn versus GSe $3,228mn and income tax expense of $50mn versus $103mn.
The company has $1.7bn of incremental capital opportunity. $700mn of that capex is now approved from the TIDE transmission project, which was selected for the ISO-NE LTTP within the quarter.

On the FERC ROE proceedings, GS looks for a decision by November 30th. If FERC does not rule, the transmission ROE of 11.39% would be effective. A refund appeal is also pending with the D.C. Circuit Court.
FFO/Debt rose to 15.4% (S&P) and 16.1% (Moody's) from 14.3% and 15.7% in March 2026, which GS cites as balance sheet progress.
GS expects the call to focus on FERC ROE proceedings, Revolution Wind and incremental capital opportunities, and regulatory updates on the CL&P rate case and storm cost securitization.

GS's suggested call questions cover pushback on the CL&P rate case and affordability, remaining risks to storm cost securitization timing and cost in CT, and how the company would use a transmission ROE above the 9.57% assumed in its plan.
GS rates ES Buy with a $80 12-month price target, 13.5% upside from the $70.46 close on 4 Nov 2026. It describes solid execution and several positive regulatory catalysts ahead.

market_movers.rationale: GS sees solid execution and several positive regulatory catalysts ahead, including the FERC ROE decision and the CL&P rate case. The target uses 15.5x P/E on Q5-Q8 estimates.
